items.title: Rice team turns toxic 'forever chemicals' into battery-grade lithium

featured_image.name: Lithium helps reduce PFAS to reusable fluorine

items.description: Two recent studies are offering cleaner paths to securing lithium — one by repurposing toxic "forever chemicals" to pull lithium from brine, the other by using nothing more than carbon dioxide and water to recycle spent batteries. Together, the advances address twin pressures facing the clean energy transition: growing demand for battery-grade lithium and the environmental toll of obtaining it.

items.title: NASA begins assembling Dragonfly rotorcraft for Titan mission

featured_image.name: NASA's Dragonfly Mission Begins Rotorcraft Integration ...

items.description: NASA's Dragonfly mission has officially entered its integration and testing phase, a milestone that marks the beginning of assembling the nuclear-powered rotorcraft that will one day fly across the surface of Saturn's moon Titan. The work is underway in clean rooms at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory in Laurel, Maryland, where engineers are building the car-sized, eight-rotor drone ahead of a planned 2028 launch.[1]

items.title: Israel plans military base in Somaliland to counter Houthis

featured_image.name: Israel to build base in Somaliland to target Houthis, says ...

items.description:
As war with Iran continues, Israel is quietly laying the groundwork for a military and intelligence presence in Somaliland, the breakaway East African territory it recognized in December, with the goal of countering Yemen's Houthi movement from across the Gulf of Aden.

The arrangement would allow Israel to gather intelligence on and conduct operations against the Houthis, according to a Bloomberg report citing two Somaliland officials who requested anonymity. Somaliland's minister of the presidency, Khadar Hussein Abdi, confirmed the trajectory of the partnership in an interview with Bloomberg in Hargeisa. "In terms of security, we will have a strategic relationship and that encompasses a lot of things," Abdi said. "We haven't discussed with them if it becomes a military base, but definitely there will be an analysis at some point."[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump says 'practically nothing left' to target in Iran

featured_image.name: Trump delivers Iran messaging through exclusive interview spree

items.description:
President Donald Trump declared on Wednesday that American forces have nearly exhausted viable military targets in Iran, telling Axios in a five-minute phone interview that the war will end "soon" because there is "practically nothing left to target" in the country. "Little this and that… Any time I want it to end, it will end," Trump said.[1][2][3]

The remarks came as the joint U.S.-Israeli campaign, dubbed Operation Epic Fury, entered its 12th day. U.S. Central Command reported earlier this week that American forces have struck more than 5,000 targets and damaged or destroyed over 50 Iranian ships since operations began on February 28. Trump also warned Tehran he would retaliate "twenty times harder" should Iran attempt to block oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.[2][4][5]

items.title: IRGC claims strikes on ships in Strait of Hormuz, demands transit approval

featured_image.name: Cargo ship struck by a projectile in the Strait of Hormuz: UK

items.description: Three commercial vessels were struck by unknown projectiles in and around the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported, in a sharp escalation of attacks on shipping through the world's most critical oil chokepoint. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps appeared to claim responsibility for at least some of the strikes, with IRGC Navy Commander Alireza Tangsiri warning that "any vessel intending to pass must obtain permission from Iran".[1][2][3][4]
